script: Odia (Oriya), Shree-Lipi 7 family. Composers: C:\Shree-Lipi nxt\S8OriU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Ori764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes). Encoding measured: shree-ori7 (unicode-to-shree-ori7.json and shree-ori7-to-unicode.json, source font id kalinga).
coverage:
Truth: 41,470 Unicode strings that have a preferred/accepted spelling. They come from 57,500 pairs (47,175 distinct Unicode strings; 10,349 rows are quirks and the rest are alt or canonical). The pairs are 56,477 probe sequences on 1,203 probe keyboards plus 1,155 vendor-key rows from the 8 .ORI keyboards. Probe sets:
- P (gen.js, 42,433 sequences, 903 files): every consonant (33 plus ଡ଼ ଢ଼ ୟ ୱ ଵ କ୍ଷ) alone. Each one with the pending link, halant 44, half D5, link+ZWJ/ZWNJ, nukta, ra/ya/ba-phala (D1/D2/E1), the codes 51 and E0, the reph, ଂ ଁ ଃ alone and in pairs, and all 18 sign codes (ା ି ୀ ୁ ୂ ୃ େ ୈ=େ+C+ୖ ୋ=େ+C+ା ୌ=େ+C+ୗ ୖ ୗ, plus F8 F6 F7 E7 E8 E9). Each sign also followed by a tail or a reph.
- P, reph orders: after the base, after the sign, before or after a tail, before the post sign, reph-first, and ର + link/halant/half + C.
- P, phala forms with every sign, tail and reph, plus the sign-before-phala order.
- P, two-consonant clusters: C1 + link + C2 for 38x38 letters (33 consonants, ୟ ଡ଼ ଢ଼ ୱ ଵ). Each one alone, with 8 post signs and େ, with ଂ ଁ ଃ, with ra-phala, ya-phala, a pending link, a halant and a reph. Also C + link + କ୍ଷ both ways.
- P, the rest: independent vowels with tails, reph and nukta; ଓ+link+ବ (ୱ); every single code 21..FE; signs alone; the vendor conjunct slots; 7 kinds of two-syllable word probes.
- H (12,888 sequences): C1 + 44 + C2 and C1 + D5 + C2 for 36x36 letters; the 44 form also with ା ି ୁ ଂ େ, reph, ra-phala and ya-phala.
- W (1,156 sequences): C1 + link + C2 + E1 (C1୍C2୍ବ: the chart clusters ତ୍ତ୍ବ ଦ୍ଧ୍ବ ନ୍ଧ୍ବ ନ୍ଦ୍ବ ଜ୍ଜ୍ବ ଦ୍ଦ୍ବ) and C + E1 + reph/ଂ/ୋ. These are 7-only evidence: the Unicode composer writes nothing for E1. They are in ori7-only7-evidence.json, not in the truth.
- E explore set (868 sequences): evidence only.
The Odia layouts built from the 9 CHM charts produce 306 outputs; 282 have a truth entry.
Not covered:
(a) Anything that needs more than 4 codes, because a slot holds 4 codes and slots inside slots are ignored: C୍C + ୈ/ୋ/ୌ (ଅକ୍ଟୋବର), C୍C୍ର or C୍C୍ୟ + a sign (ମନ୍ତ୍ରୀ ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟା), three-consonant clusters other than C୍C୍ର/C୍C୍ୟ (ଙ୍କ୍ତ ତ୍ସ୍ନ), and reph + C୍C + sign.
(b) No 7 spelling at all, because the composer types nothing: C୍ୱ (U+0B71 after a virama: ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର ସ୍ୱାସ୍ଥ୍ୟ ବିଶ୍ୱ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ), ଵ, ୡ, ଓଁ, ୄ ୢ ୣ, ॥, × ÷, — – “ ”, + ; = [ ], the nukta on plain letters, and the Vedic marks.
(c) Unicode ya-phala ୍ଯ (U+0B2F) has no canonical spelling. The composer writes it as visible halant + ଯ (FA BE), kept as alt; Shree's own ya-phala is ୍ୟ (U+0B5F) = BF.
(d) Strings whose Unicode answer is a composer quirk, for example ର୍କ୍ରା and ର୍କୃ: the Unicode composer drops the reph after a ra-phala or after ୃ.
Syllables join by plain concatenation: 201/201 two-syllable probes match. Common words: 123 of 205 coverable words are spelled exactly by the shipped table; 14 are not coverable (7 with C୍ୱ, 7 that need 5 codes).
stability:
Every set was captured twice, in separate composer processes: P 903/903 files, H 275/275, W 25/25, vendor 8/8, explore 19/19. All pairs are identical once one quirk is normalised. Raw byte-identity is 0 files, because the 7 composer returns a random large unit count instead of 0 when it has no answer: 4902400 in one run and 5458176 in the other for the lone link code 64, and the same happens for vendor keys holding 3D 46 51 5A 64 66. verify-stability.js treats a count outside 0..60 as "no answer".

Inside each process, every file was asked twice with identical answers (#stable 1). After every LoadKbdOverlay, table 0 of SL8_DLL_DATA equalled the file (#loaded 1). Every probe file also passed the untouched-key check (V X Z 0 5 _ <).

SLNXT was not affected. The SL8_DLL_DATA dump before the first load (shmdump/start.bin: header 00 00 01, tables zero) was written back after each of the 9 runs, each time with 0 bytes different, and shmdump/final.bin equals start.bin.

Quirks:
- Unicode-composer carriers: a lone sign comes back on ' ' or '.', and the lone link gives the placeholder 'Lk'.
- The 7 composer answers on carrier byte 07 in phonetic mode (ENG/PHONETIC, 18 rows).
- The Unicode composer keeps only the first of two of ଂ ଁ ଃ (324 rows).
- It drops the reph after a ra-phala and after ୃ, drops ୃ and the link after a ra-phala, and puts the nukta after େ.
- It reads code 51 as ତ୍ only after କ, and as ି or nothing elsewhere.
- The 7 composer loses the reph struck after ି + ଂ (C E7 F3, 34 rows). For C + reph + ି it writes only the letter.
- The 7 composer writes nothing for these codes: E4 E5 E6 E7 E8 E9 EA F4 F6 F7 F8 EB EC ED DD DE DF 7B 7C 7D 7E 2B 3B 3D 5B 5D.
- Codes only the 7 composer types: E1 -> FD, 51 -> 23, E0 -> E3.
- The composers switch mode by keyboard name: INSCRIPT types E7/E8/E9 as େ + length mark; ENG/PHONETIC answer consonants with their virama form.
- Tutor layers 3 to 12 answer exactly as layer 2. The Ctrl+Shift+1 layer is not reachable through the tutor.
family:
The (3,1) cmaps of all 12 installed faces were read (fonts/family-check.json; glyphs rendered by glyph index).
- 7 faces: WORI7001, WORI7002, S0600892..S0604892 (SHREE-ORI7-0600..0604).
- 4/5/6 faces: S06000F2..S06040F2 (SHREE-ORI-0600..0604).

S06xx892 and S06xx0F2 are identical code for code in all five designs: 216 codes, same glyph ids, same raw outline bytes and advances (216/216 each).

WORI7001.TTF and WORI7002.TTF carry the same family names as S0603892/S0604892 (SHREE-ORI7-0603 and -0604), so two installed files claim one name and which one Windows picks is ambiguous. They add ₹ at 3C (217 codes, glyph ids shifted by one). Against S06030F2, 7 codes have touched-up outlines (62 67 97 A1 A3 BE C7); against S06040F2, 5 codes do (82 88 89 C6 F4). They are the same characters with the same advances (fonts/diff-wori-vs-456.png, f4.png).

Bytes 80 81 8D 8E 9D 9E have no glyph in any face. 8F (୰) and 90 (ଽ) sit on U+008F/U+0090, and every other byte 80-9F sits on its Windows-1252 code point. So the shipped table writing ୰ and ଽ at U+008F/U+0090 is correct for these fonts.

The truth uses only bytes present in every face, except 3C (₹), which only WORI7001/2 have. One table serves both families; ₹ is the only code that differs.
currentTables:
Measured with the real FontConverter. The measure harness builds FontSoftware.Core from the snapshot copy; FontConverter.cs, MappingTable.cs, ConfigLoader.cs and both ori7 tables are md5-identical to the main checkout. Tables: unicode-to-shree-ori7 (965 pairs, 2 preRules for େ/ୈ) and shree-ori7-to-unicode (224 pairs, 2 postRules). Three runs gave identical output.

FORWARD, 41,470 truth strings:
- Exact 13,408 = 32.33%; accepted 13,413 = 32.34%; 28,057 fail, 12 of them matching a Shree alt spelling.
- Without the 14,194 strings that hold ZWJ/ZWNJ: 13,413/27,276 = 49.18%.
- 14,731 rows report unmapped characters: U+200C 12,860, U+200D 1,334, ୈ 262, ୌ 262, ₹ 1, ASCII punctuation.
- By category: reph ର୍+C 0/2,510; virama+ZWJ/ZWNJ 0/11,528; e/ai/o/au 26.6%; ra-phala 37.0%; ya-phala 46.0%; C୍C 50.2%; word-final virama 30.0%; consonant+sign 95.7%; ଂ ଁ ଃ 96.4%; digits 100%.
- 20,000 random syllable joins: 5.64% exact.
- Common words: 123/205.

Failure causes (one string can have several; Unicode: ours | Shree):
- A. 14,194: ZWNJ/ZWJ written into the legacy text. କ୍‌: 4C FF FA U+200C | 4C FF FA.
- F. 7,292: the first letter's spacer FF dropped before a subjoined form. କ୍ଖ: 4C 52 | 4C FF 52.
- B. 3,839: reph written as ର + subjoined C, or F6 before the letter. ର୍କ: C0 50 | 4C FF F6; ର୍କା: C0 50 E6 | 4C FF E6 F6; ର୍କି: C0 50 E7 | 4C FF 7D.
- G. 3,253: lowering spacer 26 missing under a subjoined form. କ୍ଟୃ: 4C 75 F5 | 4C FF 75 26 F5; କ୍ଖ୍: 4C 52 FA | 4C FF 52 26 FA.
- H. 1,728: high ୁ/ୂ after a subjoined form. ୱୁ: 48 B4 EB | 48 B4 EC.
- I. 678: ନ written as 5B. ନ: 5B | 9C FF.
- L. 568: ba-phala. କ୍ବ: 4C FD | 4C FF B4.
- C. 524: ୈ/ୌ have no pair and pass through as Odia text. କୈ: U+0B48 4C FF | 7B 4C FF F0; କୌ: 4C FF U+0B4C | 7B 4C FF F2.
- N. 484: କ୍ଷ split inside clusters. ର୍କ୍ଷ: C0 50 FA CC | E4 F6.
- J. 333: ya-phala written as halant + ୟ. ନ୍ୟ: 9C FF FA DF | 9C FF BF.
- K. 290: ra-phala written as halant + ର. ନ୍ର: 9C FF FA C0 FF | 9C FF F7.
- D. 257: ୋ writes 7B after the letter. କୋ: 4C FF 7B E6 | 7B 4C FF E6.
- P. 168: େ on ଡ଼/ଢ଼ comes after the letter. ଡ଼େ: DD 7B | 7B DD.
- M. 129: ି on ଖ/ଥ/ଧ. ଖି: 51 E7 | 51 23.
- E. 118: େ after a ra/ya-phala cluster. ର୍ୟେ: F6 DF 7B | 7B DF F6.
- O. 1: ₹ passes through as U+20B9 | 3C.
- 760 other, e.g. word-final ର୍: F6 | C0 FF FA; ୟେ: DF 7B | 7B DF.
Rendered side by side (fonts/ours-vs-shree.png), these are visible errors: collisions, the reph on the wrong letter, the e-sign in the middle of the word.

REVERSE, Shree's preferred bytes back to Unicode:
- Exact 20,185/41,470 = 48.67%; same text 23,537 = 56.76%; without ZW strings 20,701/27,276 = 75.89%; all accepted spellings 23,691/42,267 = 56.05%.
- Unmapped bytes in 4,005 rows: 26 in 3,253 rows (read back as &), FF in 570 (read as ÿ, e.g. 4E FF -> କ୍ତÿ), 23 in 173 (read as #), 3C -> <.
- The visible virama FA is read as ୍, so C୍‌C (7,079 rows) and C୍‍C (1,023) come back as conjuncts C୍C.
- B4 is read as ୍ୱ where Shree writes ୍ବ (419 rows).
- The reph F6 after the letter is read as କର୍ instead of ର୍କ.
- 7B C ... ୍ୟ is read as େ before the ya-phala.

The tables' own round trip, Unicode to ours to ours, is 41,470/41,470 = 100%. That is exactly what a green round-trip test shows while the output is wrong.
keyboards:
All 8 vendor keyboards were captured key by key from their original paths (Odia has 9 CHM charts; Modular is chart-only): CRTRONIC, DOE, ENG, INSCRIPT, NEWROMA, PHONETIC, ROMA, TYPEWRIT. Each was captured in both families (U and 7), twice, on these layers:
- layer 0 (normal and shift, 74 to 92 keys each)
- layer 1 = Ctrl+Space (CRTRONIC 22, DOE 22, ROMA 19, ENG 14, PHONETIC 14, NEWROMA 13, INSCRIPT 8, TYPEWRIT 0)
- layer 2 = the composer's raw code layer (92 each)

Saved in ori-vendor-keys.json, per key: the codes it holds (slots expanded), the raw and cleaned Unicode answer, the 7 bytes and the unit counts. The raw TSVs are in capvo/ and capvo-b/. 1,155 script rows went into the truth as vendor-key rows (992 accepted, 144 phonetic/inscript-mode quirks, 18 with carrier 07).

The Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer is not exposed by the tutor: tutor layers 3 to 12 equal the raw layer (layers/TYPEWRIT.tsv). So ori-vendor-keys.json records it as the 20 chart keys that all Odia charts share, each with its internal code's answer from both composers:
- 3C (₹), 3E (।), 4B (ୠ), 68 (ଌ), 90 (ଽ), BF (୍ୟ)
- ×, ÷, —, –, [ ], ଼, ୣ, ୢ, ୄ, ଓଁ, ୱ, ॥, ୡ: the 7 composer types nothing.

layercheck.js: Ctrl+Space answers agree with the key's code in 100/110 keys for both composers. The 10 misses are the ENG/PHONETIC virama forms, where both composers agree with each other.
notes:
What blocks a perfect table:
1. Forms longer than 4 codes have no composer answer (C୍C + ୈ/ୋ/ୌ, C୍C୍ର + sign as in ମନ୍ତ୍ରୀ, three-consonant clusters). They have to come from the checked rules in ori7-patterns.txt: sign glyphs append to the cluster; after a hanging subjoined form ୁ = EC, ୂ = EE, ୃ = 26 F5, ୍ର = 26 F7, ୍ = 26 FA; the reph F6 comes last, before ଂ ଁ ଃ; syllables concatenate (201/201).
2. C୍ୱ (very common: ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର, ସ୍ୱାସ୍ଥ୍ୟ, ବିଶ୍ୱ, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ) has no Shree 7 spelling. This needs a policy: Shree writes ୱ as 48 B4 and C୍ବ as C B4, so writing C୍ୱ as C B4 is the natural choice.
3. Unicode ya-phala ୍ଯ (U+0B2F) is only spelled FA BE by the composer. Mapping it like ୍ୟ (BF) is a policy choice.
4. Some strings have two Shree spellings; both are kept as accepted:
   - ର୍ର: reph C0 FF F6, preferred, or ra-phala C0 FF F7
   - ର୍ୟ: DF F6 or C0 FF BF
   - ଧ୍ୟ: 9A or 99 BF
   - କ୍ଷ: E4 or 4C FF FA CC
   - reph and tail order: F6 F3, preferred because it renders the reph on the letter, or F3 F6
   - ର୍ at a word end: preferred C0 FF FA; the lone reph key's F6 is kept as alt
5. The 7-only codes need reverse pairs even though no Unicode composer answer exists: FD (a second ba-phala form), 23 (the hook in ଖି ଥି ଧି and ତ୍ନ = 9C FF 23), E3. ori7-only7-evidence.json has 3,850 rows of evidence.
6. WORI7001/2 share family names with S0603892/S0604892.

Other notes:
- Forward 'accepted' is dominated by the H set: 14,194 truth strings carry an explicit ZWNJ/ZWJ. Category and non-ZW figures are given separately.
- The TypingEngine was not measured in this run; only the FontConverter tables were (no UI, as instructed). The per-key vendor captures are saved for that audit.
- Nothing was edited in the main checkout. Builds ran only in cap-ori/measure, one at a time, with node reuse and shared compilation off. No processes are left running.
